completion_data.completion_summary: A connective signature layer (FormalSystem/Syntax/Connectives.lean) now carries eight primitive-operator classes and the derived operators once; the nine formula types are instances, four take generated bodies, the clause classes are mixins over it, and operator recognition reads it. Phase 9 recorded the reducibility assessment, documented the layer, and repaired the citation and README-stamp findings the earlier phases introduced.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic reanchor-lean-citations.py --by-name coverage
sapience_notes.value: finding is: `python3 scripts/reanchor-lean-citations.py --by-name --files F` re-points only a `F:NNN` citation whose declaration name is on the same line. A citation whose name sits on the previous line is left alone, and after a uniform shift it lands on a non-blank line, so C20 tier 1 of scripts/check-module-invariants.sh passes it stale. After any run, grep every citation of F and compare against the measured shift.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic reanchor-lean-citations.py range citations
sapience_notes.value: finding is: the by-name mode re-pointed a named range citation `Syntax/Formula.lean:185-186` to `205-206`, the declaration's `def` line and the blank line after it, where the shifted docstring range was 193-194. The C20 run that followed did not report the blank range end. Range citations need a hand check after the tool runs.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic readme-lint.sh staleness rule
sapience_notes.value: finding is: scripts/readme-lint.sh dates a directory by `git log -1 --format=%cs -- <dir>`, which is recursive. A one-line comment edit in a subdirectory file makes every ancestor README with a non-baselined stamp a stale-date finding, so a citation repair in Metalogic/WeakCanonical/DenseModelSurgery/ touches the staleness of Metalogic/WeakCanonical/README.md. A plan that edits a file must list each ancestor README whose stamp is not on scripts/readme-date-baseline.txt.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic README Last-verified stamps hide prose drift
sapience_notes.value: finding is: all four READMEs restamped at the close of the connective-signature work had prose that disagreed with their directories: SeparationZ's hand-written line counts were wrong on nine of thirteen files, Expressiveness described its generated inventory table as hand-written and listed imports the directory does not have, and SoundnessLemmas listed two of six importers. readme-lint.sh checks the date, not the content; moving a stamp without reading the README certifies stale prose.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic verify-all.sh vs check-module-invariants.sh
sapience_notes.value: finding is: scripts/verify-all.sh runs check-module-invariants.sh with --no-build, so C14's #print axioms half and C16's env-linter batches are not in it. On branch dev/m7-ladder-continuation at 2026-11-25 the full script fails on C14 (baseline row RaySummary.exists_kappa_collision_cellAt_ne_at_K4_clip not produced) and C16 (six entries above ceiling in BimodalLibTest, ProofModeTemporalTest and four BimodalTools modules) while verify-all.sh reports the script as passing.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic verify-touched.sh in a stale deploy
sapience_notes.value: finding is: with the deployed .claude/ tree stale for the core extension, `bash .claude/scripts/verify-touched.sh` selected 142 suites, ran about 35 minutes and failed 16 of them in agent-tooling suites citing files missing under agent-system/extensions/, independent of which Lean or README files were touched. A foreground Bash call is cut near 180 s, so it has to be detached and polled by PID.
